# Normal Exposure

> > Notes on a career in cinematography from Richard Crudo, ASC — exploring the art, craft, and philosophy of visual storytelling

Normal Exposure is the personal blog of Richard Crudo, ASC, former president of the American Society of Cinematographers. The site features technical insights, lighting diagrams, film history, and reflections on the balance between technology and artistry in cinematography, drawing from decades of professional experience and relationships with legendary cinematographers like Conrad Hall, Gordon Willis, and Vittorio Storaro.

## Key Topics

- ASC (American Society of Cinematographers)
- Richard Crudo, ASC
- Cinematography philosophy and workflow
- Lighting techniques and diagrams
- Film history and preservation
- Digital vs film transition
- Technology vs artistry debate
- Color grading and DI workflow
- Legendary cinematographers (Conrad Hall, Gordon Willis, Vittorio Storaro)
- Post-production processes
- AI impact on cinematography
- Technicolor and film formats
- Camera technology evolution
- Visual storytelling craft

## Lighting Techniques & Technical Guides

- [LIGHTING DIAGRAM #1 - PRESUMED INNOCENT](https://normalexposure.com/lighting-diagram-1-presumed-innocent): Gordon Willis courtroom lighting setup for Presumed Innocent
- [LIGHTING DIAGRAM #72 - THE FLAMINGO KID (1984)](https://normalexposure.com/lighting-diagram-72-the-flamingo-kid-1984): Continuity matching techniques for day exterior with Matt Dillon
- [FACTORS THAT WILL INFLUENCE HOW YOU LIGHT, PART 1](https://normalexposure.com/factors-that-will-influence-how-you-light-part-1): Lighting planning factors: location, ISO, mood, and workflow considerations
- [TESTING...TESTING...](https://normalexposure.com/testing-testing): Sensor testing and exposure methodology from ASC Manual chapter
- [MORE FROM MODERN SCREEN](https://normalexposure.com/more-from-modern-screen-part-3): Gregg Toland's Citizen Kane lighting techniques from 1940s article

## Cinematography Philosophy & Craft

- [ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IS COMING FOR YOU](https://normalexposure.com/artificial-intelligence-is-coming-for-you): AI's impact on cinematography and creative authenticity with Pinar Demirdag
- [TECHNOLOGY IS THE MEANS, NOT THE END - PART 2](https://normalexposure.com/technology-is-the-means-not-the-end-part-2): Richard Crudo's perspective on technology vs artistry in cinematography
- [THELONIOUS MONK ON HOW TO PLAY A GIG, PART 3](https://normalexposure.com/thelonious-monk-on-how-to-play-a-gig-part-3): Thelonious Monk's wisdom applied to cinematography leadership
- [NOW HEAR THIS!](https://normalexposure.com/now-hear-this): Walter Hill quote and reflections on AI, storytelling, and optimism
- [A WAY OF SEEING](https://normalexposure.com/a-way-of-seeing): Antonioni's L'Avventura cinematography analysis with Aldo Scavarda

## Post-Production & Digital Workflow

- [PARTY TIME](https://normalexposure.com/party-time): Color correction workflow with DI colorist Bryan McMahan at Roundabout
- [ISN'T PHOTOSHOP COOL?](https://normalexposure.com/isnt-photoshop-cool): Photoshop and DI workflow compared to traditional darkroom techniques
- [ARCHIVING AND RESTORATION](https://normalexposure.com/archiving-and-restoration): Film preservation with Rob Hummel and DOTS technology discussion

## Film Analysis & Reviews

- [CAMERIMAGE](https://normalexposure.com/camerimage): CAMERIMAGE festival review from Toruń, Poland with Marek Zydowicz
- [THE CROWN, AGAIN](https://normalexposure.com/the-crown-again): Netflix's The Crown Season 6 cinematography review by Adriano Goldman
- [INCUBUS (1966)](https://normalexposure.com/incubus-1966): Conrad Hall's B&W cinematography in Esperanto horror film with Shatner
- [WICKED, WICKED (1973)](https://normalexposure.com/wicked-wicked-1973): 1973 duo-vision split-screen film review by Richard L. Bare

## Camera & Film Technology History

- [AMAZING...](https://normalexposure.com/amazing): Arthur Ball's 2-strip Technicolor camera history at ASC Clubhouse
- [HOW DID I MISS THIS ONE?](https://normalexposure.com/how-did-i-miss-this-one): Mitchell Sportster 16mm high-speed camera history and specs
- [KALVAR, aka VESICULAR FILM](https://normalexposure.com/kalvar-aka-vesicular-film): Kalvar vesicular film history and development process at MGM
